title: Story of the Door
question: Today, can Mr. Utterson learn who holds the key to the sinister door?
light: low sun from the west, deep black shadows
palette: soot black, gaslight amber, bruise violet, bone white, wet-cobble grey
motif: the blistered door and the bright key that opens it

night_corner.described: A crossroads of two narrow London streets at three o'clock of a black winter morning. Tall soot-dark brick terraces line both streets, every window shuttered and dark. Cast-iron gas lamps stand at intervals along each kerb, their flames burning yellow; the nearest lamp stands on the corner itself, throwing hard yellow light down from the upper right onto the wet cobbles and long black shadows toward the lower left. The cross street runs away downhill between its own row of lamps. Granite kerbstones, black iron railings before the basement areas, and an iron drain grating at the corner complete the junction. A black night sky hangs above the rooftops. Lamplight glows through the window at the LEFT, deep shadow.
night_corner.route: along the eastward street from its west end to the corner lamp, where the cross street meets it
night_corner.geometry: The establishing wide looks along the eastward street from its west end at head height. The corner gas lamp stands at the RIGHT third, the full height of the frame from kerb to top edge. The eastward street recedes to the CENTRE, its lamps shrinking to small yellow points along the far half. The cross street opens at the LEFT edge, sloping away downhill, its terraces a dark wedge filling the left third. Wet shining cobbles fill the BOTTOM quarter of the frame.
night_corner.ambience: a hush of empty streets, gas hissing in the lamps, a dog barking far off
night_corner.place_state: three o'clock of a black winter morning, every street lamp lit, wet cobbles shining, every window shuttered and dark

night_door.described: A small London by-street at night, its row of shop fronts closed behind freshly painted shutters with polished brass rails. Two doors from the corner the row breaks at the entry of a court, and there a two-storey block thrusts its gable forward: a blind upper wall of discoloured plaster above a single blistered, stained door set in a shallow recess with three worn stone steps. Knife scratches score the door mouldings and black match-streaks mark its panels; the keyhole plate shines bright brass. A gas lamp on the kerb throws yellow light from the left across the door and the steps, casting black shadows into the recess at the right.
night_door.route: across the by-street from the kerb lamp to the door steps
night_door.geometry: The wide faces the door square-on from the opposite kerb at head height. The blistered door stands at the CENTRE, a third of the frame's height, its recess dark. The blind gable wall fills the TOP half above it. Shuttered shop fronts run along the LEFT third toward the corner; the court entry is a black gap at the RIGHT edge. The kerb gas lamp stands at the LEFT edge, half the frame's height. Wet cobbles fill the BOTTOM quarter.
night_door.crowd: five townsfolk in shawls and nightcaps, the child's family and the doctor, shouting and pressing in a ring by the kerb lamp
night_door.ambience: a cold night hush, gas hissing in the kerb lamp, women shouting near the corner
night_door.place_state: four o'clock of a black winter morning, the kerb gas lamp lit, the shop shutters closed, the cobbles wet, the door shut in its dark recess

street_day.described: A small London by-street on a Sunday afternoon, clean and bright against its dingy neighbourhood. Shop fronts with freshly painted green and cream shutters, polished brass handles and gleaming window glass run along both sides. Two doors from the corner on the left-hand side the row breaks at the entry of a court, where a sinister two-storey block thrusts its gable forward: a blind forehead of discoloured plaster above a single blistered, stained door in a shallow recess with three worn steps. Low afternoon sun falls from the left along the street, lighting the shop brasses and throwing the recess into black shadow.
street_day.landmark: the blistered door under its blind gable
street_day.route: east along the far pavement of the by-street until abreast of the door
street_day.geometry: The wide looks diagonally across the by-street from the far pavement at head height, facing east. The blistered door and its gable stand at the RIGHT third, the gable reaching the TOP edge, the door a third of the frame's height. Bright shop fronts run along the LEFT half toward the corner. The far pavement crosses the BOTTOM quarter in the foreground. The street recedes to the CENTRE, where the corner turns away in sunlight.
street_day.crowd: two distant figures in Sunday dress strolling at the far end of the street
street_day.ambience: Sunday quiet, church bells far off, sparrows, boots on the flagstones
street_day.place_state: a bright Sunday afternoon, the shop shutters freshly painted and open, the brasses shining, the by-street nearly empty

door_step_day.described: The pavement directly before the sinister door on the by-street, seen close. The door is blistered and stained dark brown, its lower panels streaked black where matches have been struck, its mouldings scored by knife cuts; a brass keyhole plate at its right edge is rubbed bright. Three worn stone steps lead up into the shallow recess. Above, the blind gable wall of discoloured plaster rises to the eaves, and to the right a narrow court entry opens in shadow. Low afternoon sun falls from the left across the flagstones and casts the recess and the court into deep black shadow.
door_step_day.landmark: the brass keyhole plate on the door
door_step_day.route: along the pavement from the door steps east toward the shop fronts
door_step_day.geometry: The wide stands on the pavement east of the door at head height, looking back west along the frontage. The door and its recess fill the LEFT third, the door two thirds of the frame's height. The blind plaster wall fills the TOP third above it. The pavement runs from the BOTTOM edge toward the CENTRE, where sunlit shop fronts recede toward the corner. The court entry is a black slot at the LEFT edge beyond the door.
door_step_day.ambience: Sunday quiet, sparrows on the gutters, a church bell far off, wind along the court
door_step_day.place_state: a bright Sunday afternoon, the door shut in its recess, the brass keyhole plate rubbed bright against the stained paint

walk_on_day.described: A broad London street beyond the by-street on a Sunday afternoon. Grey stone terraces with tall sash windows and black iron railings line both pavements; their front steps are whitened and their brass bell pulls shine. Shallow stone steps rise to each panelled front door. Plane trees stand at intervals along the kerb, their bare branches black against a pale sky. A single cast-iron gas lamp stands on the near kerb. Low afternoon sun falls from the left down the length of the street, laying long blue-black shadows from the trees and railings across the flagstones toward the right.
walk_on_day.landmark: the gas lamp on the near kerb
walk_on_day.route: east along the near pavement from the gas lamp down the street
walk_on_day.geometry: The wide looks east down the street from the near pavement at head height. The gas lamp stands at the LEFT third, the full height of the frame. Grey terraces fill the RIGHT third, receding toward the CENTRE. Black iron railings line the terraces at the RIGHT edge. The pavement runs from the BOTTOM edge into the distance at the centre, where the plane trees shrink to small dark shapes. Pale sky fills the TOP quarter between the rooflines.

walk_on_day.ambience: Sunday stillness, distant church bells, wind in bare plane branches, a carriage far off
walk_on_day.place_state: a bright Sunday afternoon, the street broad and nearly empty, long shadows on the flagstones

shots.frame: Medium close on the small man (pale smooth cheeks, soft black felt wideawake hat) at the blistered door in its recess, his lean, corded, knuckly pale hands turning a key in the bright brass keyhole plate under the yellow kerb lamp.

The blistered door panels fill the LEFT third in yellow lamplight; black shadow fills the recess at the RIGHT edge.

shots.why: Shows the protagonist: austere, tolerant, the last good influence of downgoing men.

shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the lawyer's gaunt, rugged, unsmiling face at the CENTRE, his head half the frame's height, lifted toward the TOP edge. shots.end: The lawyer's face at the CENTRE tilted up, jaw set, his fingers on a white button in the BOTTOM third, the plaster wall at the LEFT third and the TOP edge.
source: A very good rule, too
shots.turn: agreement -> private resolve
shots.why: Silent reaction: Utterson agrees aloud and studies the house in silence.

shots.frame: Insert on the brass keyhole plate rubbed bright on the blistered door as the man about town's black walking cane tip comes down beside it.
shots.motion: The camera tracks sideways to the right, past the stained panel, across the whole shot; the black walking cane tip lowers beside the keyhole; the cane tip taps against the stained panel.
shots.camera: At the door at waist height, close, a 100mm lens; low sun from the LEFT.

shots.end: The bright brass keyhole plate at the CENTRE on the stained brown panel, the black cane tip tapping beside it at the RIGHT third, knife-scored mouldings at the LEFT third, match-streaks in the BOTTOM third.

sounds.sound: a cane tip tapping on old wood

source: There are three windows looking on the court on the first floor
shots.turn: a door -> a house that hides its life
shots.why: The motif up close: one bright lock in a neglected face.

shots.frame: Wide down the broad Sunday street as the lawyer (long black double-breasted overcoat with six white buttons) and the man about town (mid-grey long frock coat with black lapels) walk at a walking pace east past the gas lamp on the near pavement.
shots.motion: The camera rises above the two walkers, looking down over the broad street and its plane trees across the whole shot; the lawyer walks with his head bowed; the man about town swings his cane a step ahead of him.
shots.camera: On the near pavement at head height behind the gas lamp, a 28mm lens; low sun from the LEFT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the two walkers in the BOTTOM half at the CENTRE, the lawyer nearer and taller, the man about town a step ahead and smaller. shots.end: A high view of the broad street, the two walkers small at the CENTRE on the near pavement, long shadows across the flagstones, the lamp top at the LEFT third.
shots.crowd: three distant Sunday walkers on the far pavement, strolling
source: The pair walked on again for a while in silence
shots.turn: the door left behind -> the tale working in Utterson
shots.why: The walk resumes; Utterson's weight of thought sets up his choice.

shots.frame: Medium close over the near shoulder and back of the head of the man about town (dove-grey top hat with a wide brown hatband) toward the lawyer (gaunt, rugged, unsmiling face, black bowler hat with a pale grey band) as he stops and turns to him on the pavement.
shots.motion: The camera holds over the man about town's shoulder across the whole shot; the lawyer stops and turns to face the man about town; the lawyer lifts his hand toward the man about town as he asks.
shots.camera: On the pavement at shoulder height behind the man about town, a 50mm lens; low sun from the LEFT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the lawyer's gaunt face at the CENTRE, his head a third of the frame's height. The man about town's mid-grey shoulder and the back of his dove-grey top hat fill the LEFT third in the foreground. Grey terraces and black railings stand behind the lawyer at the RIGHT third.
shots.end: The lawyer at the CENTRE facing the camera, hand raised, the man about town's shoulder at the LEFT third, the terraces at the RIGHT third.
source: I want to ask the name of that man who walked over the child.
shots.turn: discretion -> the lawyer chooses to ask
shots.why: The turn: Utterson breaks their rule and demands the name of Enfield.

shots.frame: Medium close on the man about town (a heavy jaw and a lined face, dove-grey top hat with a wide brown hatband) giving the name on the sunlit pavement.
shots.motion: The camera holds a locked-off frame across the whole shot; the man about town grimaces as he speaks; his gloved hand grips the cane head; he glances back over his shoulder toward the RIGHT edge.
shots.camera: On the pavement at chest height, two paces off, a 50mm lens; low sun from the LEFT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the man about town's heavy jaw and lined face at the CENTRE, his head a third of the frame's height. His black-gloved hand grips the cane head in the BOTTOM third. A bare plane tree stands behind him at the LEFT third; grey terrace railings stretch along the RIGHT edge.
shots.end: The man about town at the CENTRE, his face turned over his shoulder toward the RIGHT edge, his gloved hand on the cane head in the BOTTOM third, the plane tree at the LEFT third.
source: It was a man of the name of Hyde.
shots.turn: a nameless brute -> a man called Hyde
shots.why: The answer: the keyholder has a name.

shots.frame: Medium close on the lawyer (gaunt, rugged, unsmiling face, black bowler hat with a pale grey band) taking in the name in silence.
shots.motion: The camera tilts up from the gaunt to the rugged, across the whole shot; the lawyer lowers his head under the bowler brim; his eyes close for a breath; his chest lifts in a long breath.
shots.camera: On the pavement at chest height, two paces off, a 50mm lens; low sun from the LEFT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the lawyer's gaunt, rugged, unsmiling face at the CENTRE, his head a third of the frame's height. The six white buttons of his overcoat run down the BOTTOM third; a black iron railing crosses behind him at the LEFT third; long tree shadows stretch along the RIGHT edge.
shots.end: The lawyer at the CENTRE, head lowered under the bowler brim, eyes shut, his chest risen under the six white buttons in the BOTTOM third, the railing at the LEFT third.
source: Mr. Utterson again walked some way in silence and obviously under a weight of consideration.
shots.turn: a question -> a dread confirmed
shots.why: Silent reaction: the name has gone home.

shots.frame: Close on the lawyer (gaunt, rugged, unsmiling face, lank grey hair, white at the sides) confessing what he knows.
shots.motion: The camera holds a locked-off frame across the whole shot; the lawyer turns his face toward the RIGHT edge; his brows draw down; his hand lifts to his coat front as he speaks.
shots.camera: On the pavement at eye height, a pace off, an 85mm lens; low sun from the LEFT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the lawyer's gaunt face at the CENTRE, his head half the frame's height, lank grey hair white at the sides under the black bowler hat. A grey stone terrace fills the RIGHT third behind him; sunlight falls from the LEFT edge onto his cheekbone.
shots.end: The lawyer's face at the CENTRE turned toward the RIGHT edge, brows drawn down, his hand at his coat front in the BOTTOM third.
source: it is because I know it already
shots.turn: a listener -> a man who already knows the drawer
shots.why: Payoff: Utterson knows the respectable name; the tale has gone home.

shots.frame: Medium close on the man about town (a heavy jaw and a lined face, dove-grey top hat with a wide brown hatband) answering with sullen force.
shots.motion: The camera holds a locked-off frame across the whole shot; the man about town's heavy jaw tightens; he jabs his cane back toward the west; his lined face flushes as he speaks.
shots.camera: On the pavement at chest height, two paces off, a 50mm lens; low sun from the LEFT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the man about town's heavy jaw at the CENTRE, his head a third of the frame's height. His black walking cane angles across the BOTTOM third in his gloved hand. The gas lamp post stands behind him at the LEFT third; grey terraces recede at the RIGHT third.
shots.end: The man about town at the CENTRE with his cane pointed toward the LEFT edge, his face flushed, the lamp post at the LEFT third.
source: I saw him use it not a week ago.
shots.turn: an old story -> a present danger: he has the key still
shots.why: The key is still in Hyde's hand this week.

shots.frame: Medium close on the lawyer (gaunt, rugged, unsmiling face, long black double-breasted overcoat with six white buttons) sighing deeply beside the gas lamp post.
shots.motion: The camera tilts up from the gaunt to the rugged, across the whole shot; the lawyer's shoulders rise and fall in a deep sigh; he turns his face toward the RIGHT edge; his hand comes down from his coat front.
shots.camera: On the pavement at chest height, two paces off, a 50mm lens; low sun from the LEFT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the lawyer's gaunt, rugged, unsmiling face at the CENTRE, his head a third of the frame's height under the black bowler hat. The gas lamp post rises behind him at the LEFT third; a bare plane tree and grey terraces stand at the RIGHT third; his hand rests at his coat front in the BOTTOM third.
shots.end: The lawyer at the CENTRE, his face turned toward the RIGHT edge, shoulders lowered, his hand at his side in the BOTTOM third, the lamp post at the LEFT third.
source: Mr. Utterson sighed deeply but said never a word
shots.turn: a hard truth -> a burden taken on in silence
shots.why: Silent reaction after the exchange: Utterson takes Enfield's news without a word.

shots.frame: Close on the lawyer (gaunt, rugged, unsmiling face, black bowler hat with a pale grey band) accepting the bargain.
shots.motion: The camera holds a locked-off frame across the whole shot; the lawyer nods once as he speaks; the corner of his unsmiling mouth softens; his hand reaches forward toward the BOTTOM RIGHT.
shots.camera: On the pavement at eye height, a pace off, an 85mm lens; low sun from the LEFT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the lawyer's gaunt, rugged, unsmiling face at the CENTRE, his head half the frame's height. The pale grey band of his bowler crosses the TOP edge; a sunlit black railing stretches behind him at the LEFT third; grey stone fills the RIGHT third.
shots.end: The lawyer's face at the CENTRE, mouth softened, his hand reaching into the BOTTOM RIGHT corner, the railing at the LEFT third.
source: With all my heart
shots.turn: a secret shared -> a secret sealed
shots.why: Utterson agrees aloud while keeping his own counsel.

shots.frame: Medium two-shot on the near pavement as the lawyer (long black double-breasted overcoat with six white buttons) and the man about town (mid-grey long frock coat with black lapels) shake hands under the gas lamp.
shots.motion: The camera holds a locked-off frame on the two men across the whole shot; the lawyer's hand clasps the man about town's black-gloved hand; the man about town lifts his chin toward the lawyer; their joined hands pump up and down between them.
shots.camera: On the pavement at head height, four paces off, a 40mm lens; low sun from the LEFT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS their two hands meeting at the CENTRE. The lawyer stands at the LEFT third, taller, his head a quarter of the frame's height; the man about town stands at the RIGHT third, his head a fifth of the frame's height. The gas lamp post rises behind them at the LEFT edge; plane trees recede at the TOP RIGHT.
shots.end: The two men at the LEFT and RIGHT thirds, hands clasped at the CENTRE, the lamp post at the LEFT edge, long shadows across the BOTTOM quarter.
source: I shake hands on that
shots.turn: two men talking -> two men bound to silence
shots.why: Silent locked two-shot after the exchange: the handshake seals the bargain.

shots.frame: Medium on the blistered door in its recess as a ragged tramp crouched on its top step strikes a match on its stained panel.
shots.motion: The camera pulls back from the crouching tramp, widening to show the whole door and its blind wall across the whole shot; the tramp drags the match along the panel; the flame flares and smokes beside the keyhole.
shots.camera: On the pavement at head height, three paces from the steps, a 50mm lens; low sun from the LEFT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS a ragged tramp crouched whole in the door recess at the CENTRE, his patched brown coat, his knees and his boots on the top step, a battered cap pulled low, his raised arm striking a match on the stained door panel beside the bright brass keyhole plate. Three worn stone steps fill the BOTTOM third; the blind plaster wall fills the TOP third above the door.
shots.end: The whole blistered door at the CENTRE under the blind plaster wall, a fresh black streak on the panel, the match flame at the RIGHT third, the steps in the BOTTOM third.
shots.crowd: one tramp in a ragged coat striking a match on the panel
source: I shake hands on that, Richard.
shots.turn: a sealed pact -> the door still keeps its secret
shots.why: The world's answer: the door stands as before, its key elsewhere.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Only one man holds the key to this door.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Each Sunday, two kinsmen walked London in silence.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Utterson drank gin alone, yet ruined men found in him their last friend.

lines.speaker: richard_enfield
lines.text: Did you ever remark that door? It holds a very odd story.

lines.speaker: gabriel_john_utterson
lines.text: Indeed? And what was that?

lines.speaker: richard_enfield
lines.text: Three o'clock of a black winter morning, street after street lit, and empty as a church.

lines.speaker: richard_enfield
lines.text: They ran into one another.

lines.speaker: richard_enfield
lines.text: And the man trampled calmly over the child's body and left her screaming on the ground.

lines.speaker: richard_enfield
lines.text: I collared my gentleman. He gave me one look, so ugly it brought out the sweat on me.

lines.speaker: richard_enfield
lines.text: We swore to make his name stink from one end of London to the other.

lines.speaker: edward_hyde
lines.text: No gentleman but wishes to avoid a scene. Name your figure.

lines.speaker: richard_enfield
lines.text: Gold, and a cheque.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Next morning the bank paid the cheque. Enfield named the place Black Mail House.

lines.speaker: gabriel_john_utterson
lines.text: Who signed it? Does he live there?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Enfield kept one rule: the more a thing looked like Queer Street, the less he asked.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They walked on; Utterson weighed the tale.

lines.speaker: gabriel_john_utterson
lines.text: I want to ask the name of that man who walked over the child.

lines.speaker: richard_enfield
lines.text: It was a man of the name of Hyde.

lines.speaker: gabriel_john_utterson
lines.text: I do not ask the other party's name. I know it already.

lines.speaker: richard_enfield
lines.text: He has the key still. I saw him use it not a week ago.

lines.speaker: gabriel_john_utterson
lines.text: With all my heart, Richard.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The door kept its secret; Hyde kept the key.
